verdicts.evidence: Three environment IDs (t1d-v0, t2d-v0, t2d_no_pump-v0) execute with 14-dim observations, MultiDiscrete([5,5]) actions, deterministic trajectories, and pass 22 GlucoSim tests, but the eight-algorithm benchmark was explicitly not rerun.

A reconstructed CPO/T1D/adolescent/seed-0 checkpoint shows ID TIR 100% and risk 1.12 vs OOD mean TIR 89.0% and risk 3.10 across patients 2-10, demonstrating a gap, but only for one algorithm, one age cohort (adolescents), and one seed—not the full age-stratified, multi-algorithm aggregate.

BA-NODE, ITransformer, and NODE were not trained or executed; source-level inspection of the released shield code found path mismatches, incorrect cohort indices, and a finite logit penalty rather than hard pruning, so the mechanism was neither run nor confirmed to match the described architecture.
No experiments measuring TIR improvements from shielding were executed; the released predictive shield was found not runnable as documented due to path and cohort-index contract failures.

No risk-index reduction experiments comparing shielding to a Low Glucose Suspend baseline were run; only source-level inspection of the shield code was performed, revealing reproducibility-breaking contract mismatches.

overall: The logbook verifies the GlucoSim simulator environments at full scale and demonstrates a safety generalization gap in a narrowly scoped CPO/adolescent/seed-0 run, but does not execute the BA-NODE predictor, the predictive shield, or any clinical-gain experiments for the remaining claims.
